content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I appreciate any help you can provide. I'm new to [product_name] and noticed something strange after downloading the diagram to the device. In simulation, everything works correctly, but after the program is downloaded, the device changes the mode for input 1. In the diagram, it's set up to operate as a momentary switch, but after downloading, it switches to a standard switch mode. Any advice would be helpful. The diagram is attached. Thank you.

The configuration for an input is used only for simulation purposes. When used in real-world applications, the input functions according to the connected hardware—whether that's a switch, push button, or similar device. If a switch is connected, the input will operate as a switch. If a momentary switch is connected, it will function accordingly.

Thank you [user_name] for the guidance. How can I monitor a normally closed input? In the diagram, you can see that if the input remains open for more than a set period, the output closes the relay and activates an alarm in the building. Again, I appreciate your help.
What is actually connected to the input? Is it a window contact for an alarm system? When the input is in its proper state, is it open or closed?

It's a magnetic sensor, installed on a door for an alarm system. Under normal conditions, the contact should remain closed. I retested and now it's working correctly—the issue was with how I connected the sensor. Thank you so much [user_name] for your help.

analysis.insight_summary: The user experienced uncertainty regarding input mode configuration in [product_name] after program download. They expected that the input mode selected during simulation (momentary switch vs. switch) would transfer to the physical device, but found that this is not the case. Another community member clarified that simulation options do not carry over to hardware, and that the physical input depends on the connected device. The original issue was eventually identified as a wiring problem rather than a software or configuration error.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expected input mode selections made within [product_name] simulation to persist after transferring the project to the device. They also want to reliably monitor and react to the state of a normally closed input for accurate detection of real-world events.
